resolved_conflicts.explanation: Wikipedia says torn down and the Forest Lookouts page says removed. The wording differs but both mean the tower is gone.

A 1965 Coast and Geodetic Survey description says the station was recovered and is in good condition, while one of two NGS listing rows for PID CQ2989 codes its surface mark as reported destroyed (the other row codes it as no geodetic control). Neither record gives a visit date that shows which is current, so the marker's present condition is unresolved.

notes_for_editor: No source read gives the tower's construction date, builder, design, height or staffing, so the story has no built or staffing section beyond the 1915 state context. The Forest Lookouts page is mostly site navigation; its Athens content is the agency, county, township/section, status and an NGS station block. The NGS listing has two rows for PID CQ2989, coded XX (surface mark reported destroyed) and NN (no geodetic control), each for horizontal and vertical control. The listing's own legend defines both codes, but nothing in it says which row is current. The firetower.org six-site list was read in full and does not include Athens. The 'nothing to visit' claim was removed from the story; access stays unset. The brief's coordinates (32.6576, -93.0597) match the Wikipedia point to four decimals, but the Forest Lookouts page gives no coordinates, so the record's location source label may be wrong. Ownership 'state' in the record is not stated in any source read here. Access was not set because no source supports an access level and there is no tower to visit. The NGS name 'Athens Fire Tower LFC' could be added as an other_name.
